title: Owner reports immediate heat
text:
# BioShock 3D Bridge v0.1.5: Heat Findings

**Passport:** wakkan.bioshock3d.bridge.private
**Package:** com.wakka.omnibridge.bioshock3d (versionCode 6)
**Device in evidence:** Samsung SM-S938U (S25 Ultra), Android 16 / API 36
**Owner request (verbatim):** We've got heat issues pretty much immediately into gameplay. Help me figure out why. Current hardware absolutely shouldn't have any issues

**Scope:** Source read (BridgeController.java, BrewRuntime.java) plus the two v0.1.4 phone reports. No build, no device test, no code changes. No heat measurement exists yet.

[... selected excerpt ...]

1. The original game asks for a **2 ms timer** between frames (`SetTimer`, stored in `lastTimerDelay`). It was written for slow feature phones and runs flat out.
2. The bridge runs the game by **emulating its ARM/Thumb code in Java**, one instruction at a time (`Cpu.step()` in BrewRuntime.java).
3. Each tick runs one guest timer callback (`session.pumpTimers(1)`), then schedules the next with:
   `delay = max(1, requested - elapsed)` (BridgeController.tick)
4. A frame takes about 34 ms on average (about 76 ms recently), far longer than the 2 ms requested. The posted delay is therefore always 1 ms. The report shows 1 ms posted delay in all 912 samples.
5. The next frame is queued immediately after the previous one. There is no frame cap and no idle time, so the "BioShock original ARM" worker thread stays busy continuously.

[... selected excerpt ...]

### What it is not

- Not diagnostics, saves or report writing. Those cost about 0.2 to 3 ms each.
- Not demonstrated by the existing thermal data. The v0.1.4 reports carry only severity snapshots (LIGHT, then NONE) with no degrees, power or trend. The heat observation is valid but unquantified.
- The two reports were captured with the host paused, so they do not capture sustained gameplay.

### Side effect: input lag

Long guest frames hold the single worker thread. Key presses and releases wait behind the running frame (about 48 ms average, about 127 ms p95). This contributes to sluggish control response and shares the same root cause.
note: Historical initial heat analysis. BS15 identifies the timer-deadline defect; BS18 supplies the later measured phone trend.

title: A quick tap could disappear before the game saw it
text:
Native key lifecycle independently verified
- Keymanager vtable 0x102508: +4 query pressed 0x12C898; +0x14 press 0x147A04;
  +0x1C release 0x147A40; +0x20 last key 0x12C8BC; +0x24 cleanup 0x212E88.
- Press sets pressed[index]=1, released[index]=0 and last key = index.
- Release sets released[index]=1 and last key = 98 (sentinel); the pressed bit stays
  set until original cleanup clears pressed/released following native input.
- Independent fresh runtime probe read these exact fields before/after DOWN,
  release before callback and one callback. See native_key_fields.txt and source.
- Consequently press+release before a native callback can erase menu last key
  before a menu sees it. Serializing release after at least one naturally due
  native callback preserves an ordinary phone key press without host timer pumping.
- World pressed array queries can observe one post release sample, as native code
  explicitly defers cleanup. Do not override that lifecycle in guest memory.

title: Finding the original controls inside the data

title: A seek bug became a garbage-collector fault
text:
EARTHWORM ABI CORRECTIONS
The inherited IFile.Seek implementation used incorrect origin values and returned zero on success. Earthworm's original BREW ABI uses START=0, END=1, CURRENT=2 and returns the resulting byte position. Incorrect navigation read the data.bar directory as constants.bin, creating a malformed VM array whose data pointer reached the module start; the original native GC then faulted. Correcting seek origins and return values fixes the startup fault. No ARM instruction or game asset patch was required.

The adapted services also supply the original 240x320/depth16 device-info prefix, free bytes from the actual 16MiB guest heap, BREW3 packed version, font metrics, named BAR resource selection/path normalization, and normal sound policy. Optional carrier information is reported unavailable with the original error/size convention. The new startEarthwormSession factory accepts the original module, resource map, saves, pixel decoder and explicit diagnostic mode.

title: Keep the wait, spare the interpreter
text:
EXECUTION AND TIMING
BrewRuntime executes the original module's applet, event handler, ARM/Thumb instructions and game logic. Android supplies compatible interfaces for display/bitmaps, resources, files, input, clock, timers and media. BridgeController serializes guest execution, timers, audio callbacks and save writes on one HandlerThread. Detailed trace and diagnostic counting are off during ordinary play; explicit reports capture the current session.

Only an actually due, already registered native timer callback is pumped. Input and audio events do not pump extra timers. Native registrations retain their independent callback/data identity. The host schedules from the registration deadline, without subtracting preceding guest work a second time.

The original sleep helper at 0x0011D548 parks the worker for the requested elapsed delay instead of interpreting a busy-wait. This hook is gated by the exact original module SHA-256. The host proof preserves a 100ms elapsed wait while reducing thread CPU spent on that wait from approximately 100ms to under 1ms. This is a host measurement, not a phone thermal result. Deterministic host tests use an explicit virtual clock; Android uses real elapsed time.

BYTE-EXACT CODEC ACCELERATION
The original module and compressed resources remain unchanged. The LZMA helper at 0x00165BBC can use a derived cache only when the compressed body SHA-256, lc/lp/pb properties and requested output length all match. It writes the exact decoded bytes into the allocation made by the original runtime, then returns through the original ABI. A cache miss follows the native decoder. Original game objects and game logic still execute.

app/assets/lzma_cache.bin contains 193 unique original streams, derived from 232 pack occurrences, with 1,627,451 decoded bytes. Fifty captured native outputs matched byte-for-byte. Fourteen matched original frames through startup and the first-game menu/intro sequence validate the accelerated codec and quiet presentation path. The manifest is in evidence/lzma_cache_manifest.json; tools/prepare_codec_cache.py rebuilds the cache from the unchanged data.bar. This avoids about 243 million interpreted startup instructions.

title: A tap that lives long enough to be seen
text:
INPUT AND PRESENTATION
The multitouch D-pad retains source reference counts for touch/controller chords. The action key preserves original tap-to-whip/hook and hold-to-fire behavior. Dedicated 1/2/3 buttons supply the actual diagonal/vertical jump key codes. The complete original keypad is available.

A touch or accessibility tap released before the game polls input remains native-down through one normally scheduled native tick, then receives its release. Long holds release immediately once sampled. Re-press cancels a deferred release without a duplicate press. Background, focus loss and restart clear native held keys, including pending releases. This adds no input-driven timer callback.

The Android player scales the original framebuffer proportionally with nearest-pixel rendering and applies actual system/navigation/cutout insets. Frame snapshots follow changed pixel revisions. Native bitmap caches invalidate on changes to their exact backing byte ranges, including guest and host writes.

title: Music starts quietly, then the volume rises
text:
AUDIO
The original guest supplies decompressed MIDI/CMID bytes to IMedia. Android routes each request by SHA-256 of those exact original bytes. Ten standard MIDI files are preserved unchanged. Twenty-one CMID effects are decoded from the original IMA ADPCM samples to 16kHz mono signed 16-bit WAV, with no replacement sound or gain adjustment. tools/prepare_earthworm_audio.py regenerates and validates them; use --java-check for independent Java MIDI verification. The APK stores these assets uncompressed so AssetManager.openFd can address them.

The original game can PLAY at volume zero and raise the volume afterward. VOLUME events update the existing player in place. They preserve the PLAY serial used to guard START/DONE callbacks, so a volume change neither recreates playback nor invalidates its callback. Guest START/DONE notifications and actual original MIDI plus CMID effect payloads are covered by final acceptance and routing evidence.

title: The owner asks for inspection before a runtime exists
text:
USER'S WORDS
"Tell me what Omni misunderstood about this? Being able to read raw files is kind of a must. Otherwise I'm forced to have initial inspection happen with an AI. Which defeats the purpose. Dont give me a 14 page dissertation. Make it information I can digest"

[... selected excerpt ...]

WHAT WAS TESTED
- Input: Orcs-Elves-II_BREW_EN_Electronic-Arts-7041.zip
- Omni job status: NEEDS CONTENT OR A TOOL / blocked
- Investigation budget selected: 30 minutes
- Reported work: 191 milliseconds across three saved sessions; zero runtime tests
- Omni successfully staged four files (2,426,033 bytes) and recognized the BREW package.
- Identified game contents:
  - orcsandelves2.mod — BREW game module, 292,116 bytes
  - orcsandelves2.bar — BREW resources, 2,130,702 bytes
  - orcsandelves2.mif — BREW manifest, 3,195 bytes
  - orcsandelves2.cfg — configuration file
- The report found no matching runtime adapter, usable supplied runtime source, or relevant catalog match. It read zero source files and stopped without a deeper raw-binary/resource investigation.

THE MISUNDERSTANDING
Omni appears to treat the absence of an executable runtime as the end of useful local investigation. But being unable to EXECUTE an original game is not the same as being unable to INSPECT its original files.

WHY IT MATTERS
The user wants Omni to investigate unfamiliar games independently, before an AI-led bridge project already exists. If another AI must first examine every new game and explain its internals, Omni is dependent on the very external initial inspection it was intended to reduce.

[... selected excerpt ...]

WHAT THE EXISTING FILES COULD INFORM
Even without gameplay execution, raw inspection could look for:
- Module format, CPU architecture, entry points, and import/interface clues in the .mod
- Resource directory and recognizable graphics/audio/data in the .bar
- App identity, runtime requirements, or other metadata in the .mif and .cfg
- Uncertainty, gaps, and findings worth retaining for later execution work

These are investigation opportunities, not claims that any particular decoder or parser is already present or that these bytes are necessarily straightforward to interpret.

CORE DISTINCTION TO CARRY FORWARD
Intake and identification already worked. The missing capability is meaningful, evidence-producing RAW FILE INVESTIGATION that can continue when there is no matching runtime. Runtime discovery should unlock further experiments, not decide whether investigation itself can begin.

title: The original applet reaches its first unimplemented resource
text:
## What works, precisely
- The game's **original, unchanged** `residentevil.mod`, `residentevil.bar` and `REGenesis.mif` are embedded in a signed Android APK with verified SHA-256 values.
- The sandboxed Java ARM32 interpreter now supplies a **minimal synthetic** call environment. It runs the original module's loader route and observes a successful return code `0`, a nonzero allocated module pointer and populated module vtable after 64 guest instructions.
- A second **original game-code** phase calls the resulting IModule CreateInstance route using class ID `0x01073FCF`. The applet allocation succeeds, then initialization reaches a resource service request involving `residentevil.bar`, resource number `5006` (`0x138E`) after 812 additional ARM instructions. The interpreter halts deliberately at this unimplemented service.
- This is a **host-side execution trace** proven under test, NOT gameplay or completed AEE applet initialization. The proprietary BREW/AEE runtime, resource processing, screen drawing, dispatch loop, audio and saves are not implemented. In particular, temporary virtual-function pointers and phone dimensions are experimental—not verified BREW ABI definitions.
- APK compiles, verifies v2/v3 signatures, and includes shareable diagnostics; as of this checkpoint **APK has not been tested on the user's S25 Ultra**. No Internet permission is requested.

title: A reused runtime still needed this game’s actual contracts
text:
## ABI discoveries that must not regress
- This older game uses `EVT_APP_START=0`, STOP=1, SUSPEND=2, RESUME=3, key press=0x101, release=0x102. Rush's startup event value was wrong for this title.
- `IShell+0x4C` loads an image resource; first request is BAR ID 5006.
- `IShell+0x48` returns a raw resource buffer including its original BAR entry header; +0x50 releases it. Map/script records are not images. `+0xA4` loads media resource bytes and returns their size through a stacked out parameter.
- BAR: group count u16 at +6, groups base u32 at +8, offset table base at +16, resource count at +20. Group entries are 8 bytes. There are 117 entries: 107 PNGs, five MIDIs and five raw map/script entries.
- IDIB layout: +8 pixels, +12 palette, +16 native transparency key, +20/+22 width/height u16, +24 byte pitch u16, +26 palette size u16, +28 depth u8, +29 color scheme u8.
- Original ARM converts decoded RGB565 bitmap pixels into indexed sprite DIBs. Preserve that conversion; it establishes the transparency indices. ROP 7 uses the native key, not 'all black is transparent'.
- IDisplay BitBlt arguments: x/y/width in r1/r2/r3; height/source/sourceX/sourceY/ROP on stack. SetClip/GetClip offsets are +0x48/+0x4C; clipping is tracked per destination.
- IFile Read is +0x0C, Write +0x14; file info size lives at +8. Modes used: read=1, write-existing=2, create=4. FileMgr free-space is +0x20. The old mapping caused the false insufficient-memory startup screen.
- SYS_B+0xA8 fills the guest random-byte pool, not a zero buffer. Desktop seed is fixed for reproduction; Android reseeds before New Game. SYS_B+0x6C frees. The +0x8C platform-version query deliberately returns unspecified/zero; optional ISound class 0x01002001 is unsupported, not a pretend object.
- Shell device item 24 writes an explicit normal-audio policy. Leaving its out buffer untouched caused the game to disable music.
- IMedia: SetMediaParm +0x10; data parameter 1; volume parameter 4. GetState +0x34 returns READY=2 or PLAY=3. Play +0x18; seek +0x24. Notify callback is the original function at guest `0x00101264`; tested notification fields: command +8=4, status +16 (1 start, 2 done, 3 abort). Android start/completion calls the guest callback with object+serial guards so stale callbacks cannot target a recycled object.
- Key codes: 0=E021, numbers 1..9=E022..E02A, CLR=E030, UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT=E031..E034, SELECT=E035. This is tank movement, not a free-moving D-pad or Rush auto-fire.

title: Keep the original sprite conversion and avoid repeated work
text:
- IDIB layout: +8 pixels, +12 palette, +16 native transparency key, +20/+22 width/height u16, +24 byte pitch u16, +26 palette size u16, +28 depth u8, +29 color scheme u8.
- Original ARM converts decoded RGB565 bitmap pixels into indexed sprite DIBs. Preserve that conversion; it establishes the transparency indices. ROP 7 uses the native key, not 'all black is transparent'.
- IDisplay BitBlt arguments: x/y/width in r1/r2/r3; height/source/sourceX/sourceY/ROP on stack. SetClip/GetClip offsets are +0x48/+0x4C; clipping is tracked per destination.

[... selected excerpt ...]

## Performance changes already tested
Host draw operations update ARGB buffers and defer RGB565 guest-memory flush until the guest requests DIB access. Memory-page stamps invalidate decoded pixel/palette caches when original ARM code writes. Do not restore full-bitmap decode/re-encode on every tiny rectangle or blit: it is dramatically slower. Display pixels are still sourced from the original game.

## Evidence
`tests/Acceptance.java` boots fresh, selects New Game, advances original dialogue, turns/walks Jill, opens inventory and pause, saves through the original confirmation, then creates a fresh runtime and selects Load. It exercises suspend/resume, 10,000 additional idle callbacks, allocation reuse, original resource decoding, and unchanged in-memory MOD bytes. It does not inject gameplay RAM values or teleport Jill.

Read-only observed fields relative to the applet: mode +E4, overlay +A3, Jill grid +AD/+AE, facing +B8, floor index +118, interaction state +6EE. These are diagnostics, not host control knobs.

title: The timer was charged for work twice
text:
One HandlerThread owns native execution, timer pumping, saves, reports and all MediaPlayer callbacks. Android focus loss and lifecycle suspension stop scheduled gameplay and release input. Native background/resume events retain ordering even if the Activity changes quickly.

Timer pacing uses the deadline recorded at the actual native IShell.SetTimer call. The original Contra callback already requests max(20, 80 - native frame elapsed) milliseconds. v0.1.0 subtracted the whole Android tick time again; v0.1.1 waits only the time remaining after registration and checks that a timer is due before pumping it. Input and audio can update the queued deadline, but do not pump timers themselves. No queued tick remains when the guest has no timer.

Bitmap cache validity uses exact byte-range watches indexed by memory page, replacing whole-page versions. Writes outside a bitmap's header, backing memory and palette no longer invalidate its decoded pixels. Actual overlapping writes invalidate the cache; pointer or size changes rebind watches and released bitmaps remove them. RGB565 guest writeback remains immediate. The original executable, drawing order and guest memory format remain intact.

Production operations return independent pixel snapshots only when the framebuffer revision changes. Attach and explicit report capture retain full-frame reads. The controller retains a pending snapshot across same-revision audio results so a new image is not lost before Android receives it.

title: A bitmap is not its transform interface
text:
The supplied v0.1.1 device report records an unsupported interface cls=0x7E000001, offset 0x10, during a native timer callback. The earlier bridge returned the same bitmap object for QueryInterface(0x01001029), although that IID is ITransform. The later native transform call therefore reached an IBitmap vtable with the wrong method layout. v0.1.2 supplies a separately typed ITransform view retaining the original backing bitmap. Its native signed 8.8 matrix blit performs center rotation and mirroring with pixel-center sampling, source/destination clipping and transparent compositing. It keeps reference counts and backing DIB bytes coherent, including overlapping source/destination use. The original executable and game state are not patched.

The supplied v0.1.1 video starts after the combat freeze. It shows the stopped frame but does not capture the initial trigger. The short original first-guard host route reproduces the same fault with matching object/registers and LR00117BC0. The native matrix is [0,-256,256,0], a transparent 16x16 quarter rotation at destination (-1,17). The release runtime passes this route and further combat: original player HP100->97->94->91, pistol ammo10->6, guard HP40->24->9->0 and corpse flag, then movement Y1376->1312 with continuing timers. title: A bridge assembled from earlier discoveries
text:
## Prior-work references

The recovered Monster Hunter i v0.1.2 checkpoint supplies the DoJa model parser, software renderer and MFi translation foundation. Its bundled Snowboarding work informed the float utility adapter. DMC DeadShot v0.1.2 informed the per-contact input handling. Resident Evil Genesis v0.6.1 informed the dark teal presentation, controls and report tools. Wolfenstein RPG v0.1.0 and Doom RPG v0.1.1 informed system-bar/cutout handling; Contra 4 v0.1.1 informed completed-frame presentation, idle behavior and logging restraint. This title has its own Android package and signing identity.

title: Reuse the model parser without multiplying the camera twice
text:
Entry: `BioMain.start()` creates `b`, installs the DoJa canvas and starts its own game thread. First playable state in the observed route is `b.ah == 8`. The native logical surface is 240x320; the original game centres its 240x240 content at y=40. The bridge aspect-fits this surface and publishes only after graphics unlock.

The game uses `com.nttdocomo.ui.graphics3d` and float `util3d` APIs, whereas the previous Monster Hunter runtime uses `opt.ui.j3d`. The adapter preserves the game-supplied float transforms and uses the previous MBAC/MTRA parser. Translation and near/far values are scaled by 64 while the matrix basis uses 4096 fixed-point. Scaling the basis by an extra 64 produces oversized broken models. Keep these contracts separate.

Transform indices are row-major (translation 3, 7, 11). Multiply is postmultiply and supports self-aliasing. Float trigonometry is in degrees. `Vector3D.dot(a,b)` is static: matching the descriptor without matching invocation kind is insufficient. `verification/api-invocations.txt` records actual static/instance calls, and `api-refs.txt` records the larger constant-pool reference set.

title: Two scratchpad slots and their six-byte prefixes
text: The `.sp` archive format has a 64-byte container header followed by 2048-byte slot 0 and 115000-byte slot 1. Each slot begins with `ok` and a big-endian payload length. Preserve those slot bytes, including their six-byte prefix. The game itself opens URLs such as `scratchpad:///0;pos=6,length=2000`; URL parsing must accept comma-separated options and bound the read.

title: Sounds in scratchpad, and play means a seek position
text: Slot 1 contains 33 `melo` sound assets, not separate JAR `.mld` entries. The MFi parser handles these assets, including their PCM samples. Audio completion is DoJa event 3; event 2 means stopped. `AudioPresenter.play(int)` means a millisecond seek position. The game resumes background music using this overload. Android player operations run on a worker, with independent lanes and generation checks to discard stale requests. Spatial `Audio3D` requests are acknowledged; this version does not implement spatial effects.

title: The upstream core and original runtime inputs
text:
This directory contains the portable ExEn 2 VM, its platform-native API handlers, a small C host interface, and an Android JNI interface. It executes the supplied original `.exn` game bytecode. The Android build targets ARM64 and Android API 29 or later; ELF TLS is used by the allocator.

## Source and license

The VM and native handlers originate from [Handyplay's ExEn core](https://github.com/mohamedahmed166e/my-mre-emulator/tree/main/exen-core), commit `460b149302e9a52523bc314a37efabbee9f3d666`. The repository is distributed under AGPL-3.0; see `LICENSE-AGPL-3.0.txt`. The bridge and project modifications are supplied under the same license. Game content and original runtime firmware retain their original ownership.

[... selected excerpt ...]

The private runtime uses original ExEn runtime classes and its embedded bitmap font extracted from the stock simulator. The full executable is not included.

Source archive: [EXEN-V2 Emulator.zip](https://archive.org/download/spyro-exen/EXEN-V2%20Emulator.zip), MD5 `24275cdff33263bd4da977ae518c9a47`. Original `EXEN-V2.exe`: 405,504 bytes, MD5 `f102c98717b4d680f9a38199fb3c0421`, PE image base `0x400000`.

| Extracted asset | PE virtual address | File offset | Bytes | MD5 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Runtime classes, app `exen_builtins.bin`, copied to `assets/unk_4494F0.bin` | `0x4494F0` | `0x494F0` | 44,940 | `870bef21d6f269e3e3d91943c66de8e8` |
| `core/assets/font_5x8.bin` | `0x454DD0` | `0x54DD0` | 1,280 | `b2898698a79885529d4e9bd10455e775` |

title: Pacing, FIFO and snapshots gained in the Banjo bridge
text:
`banjo_state_size()`, `banjo_state_save(buffer, capacity)`, and `banjo_state_load(buffer, length)` support native snapshots within the same running session. These preserve image rasters, palette indices, class statics, heap objects, framebuffer, and pending input. They are separate from the game's own persistent `saveCtx` storage.

## Project modifications

- Added the C ABI host and Android JNI shim.
- Removed the upstream recurring Banjo heap census and object creation tracing. Opcode tracing stays disabled, and runtime warnings are held in a fixed buffer for an explicit report.
- Replaced the debug allocator with the freeing SMP allocator while retaining the VM's garbage collection between ticks.
- Preserved the original requested timer period; removed the upstream global 75 ms speedup.
- Added a bounded FIFO for key transitions. Brief taps and multiple touch controls arrive in order without advancing extra game ticks.
- Added a direct auxv reader so page-size and vDSO discovery work from a shared library without external libc symbols.
- Corrected native snapshot serialization to preserve decoded image pixels and palette indices. Snapshot version is 4.
- Preserve the live allocator interface when reconstructing a snapshot, so a stored process address is never reused as an allocator vtable.
- Made an instruction-budget halt observable as an aborted host tick instead of reporting a normal return.

title: A healthy empty AudioTrack was rejected

REPRODUCED ROOT CAUSE
Android MODE_STATIC AudioTrack begins in STATE_NO_STATIC_DATA (2) until its
first successful write. The previous code required STATE_INITIALIZED (1)
before writing; it rejected a valid track and never submitted any PCM.
The actual Android API34 framework reproduces the failure in

using the v0.1.0 source and Crash's original melody data, without mocking the
player, AudioTrack constructor, getState or write/play lifecycle.
Reference: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/AudioTrack
The platform audio output sink is supplied by Robolectric's stock native shadow;
this is not a physical speaker or Android-device listening test.

Accept a healthy waiting-for-data track. Submit the entire PCM16 buffer through
the supported ByteBuffer write API. Validate accepted byte count and readiness
before play. Preserve the original synthesis function exactly. Stop cancels
queued work; paused tunes retain their loaded buffer; late callbacks after close
are ignored. Keep the actual failure message in independent report snapshots.

title: Scrolling text exposed the wrong panel service
text:
V0.1.1 DEVICE-REPORTED TEXT FIX
The user supplied 1000101923.mp4 (32.105 seconds, 1080x2340) and Driv3r-Bridge-v0.1.0-report-20261016-115934-890.txt. On-device evidence shows old glyphs accumulating during text scrolling, plus text consuming the full guest display instead of the original panel. The report identifies Samsung SM-S938U / Android 17 API 37; no runtime fault, unsupported calls, image decode failures or Android audio errors. Framebuffer remains 120x160. The controls and header are visibly within the system bars in this recording.

The defect was in the host implementation of IDisplay vtable +0x30: it was incorrectly implemented as a screen rectangle query, rewriting the caller's 10,10 / 100x130 panel to 0,0 / 120x160 and skipping the requested background draw. Original caller 0x0010D050 copies its retained rectangle, invokes +0x30 with type=5 and background=0, then uses the resulting client bounds for heading/body/footer, wrap width and scrolling. The fixed observed flat filled panel draws the caller's background into the existing destination, respects the active bitmap clip, commits pixels and leaves the original client rectangle unchanged. No speculative frame styles are claimed; type 5 is the observed supported path.

A regression executes the original Quick Guide using only native inputs: DOWN then UP must restore exact initial framebuffer pixels; scrolling to the end and back to the start must do the same. The v0.1.0 runtime fails the first restoration comparison. v0.1.1 passes all 47 text checks, including rapid scroll input without extra native timer pumping. Before/after original-game PNGs and expected baseline failure are retained in evidence/text_fix/. Existing 72 native execution, 12 controller, 35 key mapping and 9 input-ownership checks pass.

The executable, BAR, MIF, key mappings, native save paths, app identity, signing key and report threading remain unchanged. The system font fallback is retained. Host tests establish the text repair; the updated APK has not been run on the user's phone here. The original video remains available as the user's supplied attachment; its identifying hash is recorded below rather than duplicating the recording inside this checkpoint.

title: The original statistics builder needed wide text formatting
text:
V0.1.2 DEVICE-REPORTED MISSION-STATISTICS STOP
Input: Driv3r-Bridge-v0.1.1-fault-20261016-124604-935.txt, Samsung SM-S938U / Android 17 API 37. The independent automatic report captured the native timer stop at SYS_B+0x3C, return address 0x0010418D, after 1,115 callbacks / 34,333,211 original ARM steps. Host/save errors are absent; image decode failures and unknown interfaces are zero. The original module, BAR and MIF hashes match preservation inputs.

The original ARM function at 0x001040F1 constructs Mission Complete statistics. At the reported call, r0 is the game's temporary wide output buffer, r1=200 is byte capacity, r2 points to the original widened BAR resource 303 (Mission #: %i), and r3 is the original mission number. Subsequent calls use resources 304/305/307-310/312-313 for time, damage, scores and totals. SYS+0x3C was unimplemented. It is now a bounded 16-bit text formatter for the observed signed decimal formats, integer field width/precision and literal %%. Arguments start in ARM r3 and continue on the guest stack. Time fields such as %2.2i:%2.2i produce 01:09; damage retains one percent sign. The service writes complete 16-bit characters within byte capacity and terminates when capacity permits. Unobserved format conversions remain explicit failures. This extends the host ABI; it does not change native mission rules, scores, progress or executable bytes.

The v0.1.1 runtime reproduces the exact missing service and return address when the preserved statistics builder is invoked after normal native first-mission initialization. The repaired builder executes all original statistics sections and renders the original panel. MissionStatsRegression passes 51 checks including that exact original builder, register/stack arguments, integer extremes, precision, percent literals and sentinel-checked full, truncated, odd, zero and one-byte capacities. Its direct ARM function invocation is a focused regression, not evidence that a mission was completed through gameplay; its displayed zero mission and score are the actual initialized game fields. No mission-completion flags or saves are manufactured. Retained evidence lives in evidence/mission_stats_fix/. Existing 72 original-execution, 47 text-scroll, 12 controller, 35 key-mapping and 9 input-ownership checks pass.

The earlier text bounds/clearing fix, original controls, Genesis presentation, timer policy, independent report writer, save handling, package and signing key are retained. v0.1.2 has not been physically tested here; complete mission-to-next-mission progression and full campaign completion remain unverified. This private checkpoint retains the input fault report and both the expected baseline failure and repaired renderer evidence.

title: Real Steering selected through original options
text:
V0.1.4 — APPROVED REAL STEERING / ICON UPDATE (2026-10-25 America/Chicago)
Inputs: user-approved control discussion, 1000103777.mp4 (30.174s, 1080x2340), Driv3r-Bridge-v0.1.3-report-20261025-192527-866.txt, supplied Gameplay UI Kit v1.1.2 and Omni finished handoff kit v1.0. The v0.1.3 report has no runtime stop and balanced 118 press/release inputs, but the default Directional preference and confusing control presentation made driving difficult. Original source, package, saves and signer were recovered from the v0.1.3 private checkpoint.

Native evidence and read-only observation
Original applet+0x25 is global mode. At mode 18, phase applet+0x94A is 4 for active play, 6 map, 8 story/tutorial and 19 pause. Do not infer an actor from phase alone. The physics object begins at applet+0x1200: type byte +1 is 5 on foot and 0..4 for vehicles. Original input function 0x0010A9D8 branches on type 5 for walking. Global preference byte applet+0x8DB is 1 Directional, 0 Real; actual vehicle flag applet+0x1257 selects handler 0x001010E0 when nonzero and 0x001011B4 when zero. Native menu index is applet+0x768, exposed by original getter 0x0010CF48. Result snapshots expose these five fields read-only and copy them with other presentation metadata. No guest-memory writes or interpreter/service changes were added for controls.

Original Quick Guide resource 171 identifies Real Forward UP/2, Reverse DOWN/8, Left LEFT/4, Right RIGHT/6; Directional reverse is SELECT/5. Native 1/3 are burnout turns, 7/9 emergency-brake turns. Original Out of Car help describes four-way movement and 0 to enter/exit, without a gun action. This evidence determines the four contexts rather than imposing a universal layout.

One-time preference setup
Driv3rSteeringSetup is a bounded state machine using only original key press/release events: Main menu index 3 (Options), Options index 2 (Control), Control index 1 (Real), CLR to main. BridgeController schedules those edges at 80ms intervals on its existing worker; no synthetic timers or direct prefs.dat edits. Manual input is disabled during the visibly labelled setup, and setup suspends while the Activity is backgrounded. Original prefs.dat changes only byte 11 from 1 to 0. Already-Real saves need no menu events. After success, private host preference bridge-controls/real-steering-v014 records completion; subsequent native Options changes are respected. Restart/exit cancel the setup callback. Native save persistence still owns the game preferences.

Controls
Driv3rControls chooses menu/walk/real/directional using the native phase, actor and actual vehicle steering flag. On context changes MainActivity clears touch owners and custom pointers, retaining registered hardware holds. Real Steering has a two-cell digital Driv3rSteeringPad: one stable pointer can slide LEFT to RIGHT, leave/reenter or cancel. Its BridgeInput source is independent of accelerator/reverse buttons; either release order leaves the other owner's input held. It is digital native-key steering, not analog conversion. Secondary burnout and skid keys are retained with accurate labels. Walking and menus use the original square four-way pad; menus have a separate CONFIRM. Directional fallback labels match the original scheme. Both panels retain the same renderer and stable control slot.

title: Older applet and typed-resource semantics
text:
Original input is upload Driv3r.rar, now retained at original_inputs/Driv3r.rar. Its BREW module is 73,776 bytes; resource BAR is 180,029 bytes; launcher MIF is 3,554 bytes. MIF and original string resource 3 agree on class ID 0x0101F0A9. Original metadata names LG VX4400; selected handset canvas is 120x160.

No game logic was recreated or patched. The actual supplied ARM instructions execute from address 0x00100000. This older AEEApplet layout stores its event handler at applet+0x1C; +0x18 is a display object. The original main handler at 0x00101CA9 uses EVT_KEY (0x100) in menus and EVT_KEY_PRESS / RELEASE in gameplay mode 0x12, read from applet+0x25. The input routine at 0x0010D490 retains pressed, held and released edges at applet+0x970/+0x974/+0x978. Short press/release pairs do not need extra guest timer pumping.

BAR lookup must include both ID and type: type 1 strings and type 6 binary/image/audio groups reuse IDs. Strings are raw Latin-1 with their full recorded length, widened by the shell service. Images include resource headers and BMP or image/z zlib-compressed BMP. The platform decodes those images while the original module's own bitmap paths continue executing. Native source-copy (2) and transparent (7) raster modes are supported on the observed path. Host text uses an embedded 6x10 system-font fallback with original requested strings, colors, clipping and alignment; handset font metrics are approximated.

Added title-exercised services include byte-order conversion (system +0x12C/+0x130), bounded wide-string copy (+0x80), old applet offset, typed resources, BMP IImage decoding, display text/color/alignment and the original filled text-frame service. Startup constructs older network-related helper objects. The observed startup URL helper request to http://rs.sorrent.com:80/rs/fe returns an explicit failure in this offline build; the original game handles that failure and reaches gameplay. No remote success, server response, entitlement or authentication state is fabricated. This is not a complete BREW implementation.

MIDI is delivered from the original SoundPlayer memory buffers, not recreated. Android MediaPlayer receives original bytes. Native audio started/completed notifications execute the guest callback. Audible Android output remains untested.

Guest events, audio notifications, native timers and saves share one game worker. Only due native SetTimer callbacks run; input, reports and audio callbacks never pump the timer. Routine tracing is off, and unchanged display revisions do not create new presentation pixel arrays. Sparse performance and battery-temperature measurements are retained in reports.

Direct report saving uses an immutable report cache refreshed at most once per second during ordinary play, plus a separate HandlerThread and MediaStore Downloads writer. A blocked-guest-lock regression proves capture and report writer dispatch do not depend on the guest worker. This fixture does not test physical MediaStore. Reports include snapshot age so a stalled worker's retained context is identifiable. Faults request an independent automatic report, also retained privately.

title: Decor before insets, fault capture before the UI
text:
Shared v1.1.0 startup defect:
BridgeGameplayUi.setupWindowInsets calls Window.getInsetsController while the
Activity is still constructing its gameplay shell, before setContentView.
PhoneWindow.mDecor can be null. This caused the immediate launch crash.

Embedded fix:
android.view.WindowInsetsController bars =
    activity.getWindow().getDecorView().getWindowInsetsController();

title: The original loop timestamp and functional log boundary
text:
FRAME SCHEDULING / BACKGROUND
The original t.run() sets a timestamp once before the loop and subtracts
that same timestamp from its 33 ms sleep budget forever. Consequently its
sleep reaches the original 5 ms minimum even while idle on a fast host.
Platform.pace() enforces the original intended ~30 Hz budget without spin
waiting. Original methods, timers and movement logic remain untouched.
The original loop emits a unique curLoop: line each iteration. A private
PrintStream hook uses that existing boundary for pacing and foreground
scheduling while dropping repetitive loop spam. This is functional code;
do not remove it as cosmetic logging cleanup. Other original log lines and
stderr are retained in bounded diagnostics. Android backgrounding calls the
original MIDlet pause at this boundary and parks the worker on a condition;
foregrounding resumes the original MIDlet. No thread suspension or polling
spin is used. The host harness verifies native MIDlet pause/resume; Android
foreground parking still needs device testing.

MIDP compatibility layer. ResidentEvilMIDlet, t and all other original

original class bytes are patched. All 123 non-class original resources are

native 40-pixel touch strip. The original touch strip is intentionally
preserved as part of original execution. Native pointer input is supported.

INPUT
The JAR's t.a(int) maps raw -3 to an alternate '*' input before consulting
getGameAction. Do not change the external left button to conventional -3.
Verified native mappings are Up=-1, Down=-2, Left=2, Right=-4, OK=-5.
Glu-Left-Key-Code=-6, Glu-Right-Key-Code=-7, Glu-Back-Key-Code=-8,
Glu-Center-Key-Code=-5. Thus external Back=-7 reaches the game's own back
handler. Number keys send their actual ASCII values. Numeric 5 is distinct

one per original render, preserving quick press/release ordering. Cancel,

title: Three pixels in a hidden keypad stop the first layout
text:
Repairs a reproduced first-layout crash in v0.1.0. The shared UI measures both control modes before drawing; the game-owned hidden keypad was a few pixels taller than its declared minimum at fractional densities. At 2.625, its 264dp declaration rounded to 693px while its five 48dp rows plus padding/gaps needed 696px. DoomControls threw Original key target too small during Android measure, after Activity.onCreate had returned.

The custom minimum now sums the same independently rounded components as the actual layout. This keeps complete 48dp targets and a square 144dp pad, preserves the live viewport and avoids switching/restarting the guest. The shared UI Kit itself remains the identical v1.1.2 JAR.

A scoped uncaught-fault recorder retains later measure/layout/Java failures with display density and font scale before the normal Android handler runs. Existing independent SAVE REPORT now includes the retained fault. Inactive scoped handler nodes are skipped during lifecycle cleanup.

title: The initial investigation lacks the separate Swerve engine
text:
RESULT
Not yet playable. No standalone APK or finished Omni bridge was produced.

VERIFIED ORIGINAL EXECUTION
The unmodified kh.mod executes AEEMod_Load and returns a real module object.
Its original CreateInstance succeeds for class 0x01026191, creating an applet
with event handler 0x0010E060. Startup requests extension class 0x0102BBFC,
which the inherited BREW host cannot provide. The game takes its own error
path. The host then fails at unimplemented IDisplay+0x10 while the original
error screen is being drawn. No accepted APP_START, title or gameplay is proven.

THE MISSING DEPENDENCY
Kingdom Hearts uses Superscape Swerve 3D as a separate BREW extension. Its
known preserved binary is swv21brew.mod. This executable and its original
descriptor are absent from the supplied Chapter 1 ZIP. swerve.m3g is a scene
asset, not the engine. The supplied checkpoints contain no matching Swerve
implementation or module. The checked Agrabah archive and BREW SDK extension
archive did not contain that engine either.

Recovering the engine is the next dependency, not proof of immediate success:
extension loading and remaining BREW calls must then be implemented and tested.
Startup also requests custom-font class 0x0100A004. The game continues after
that font request fails, then checks the engine result. Implementing error-text
rendering alone would not recover the missing engine.

title: Original LZMA wrapper and disposable decoded caches
text:
## v0.1.4 original loader acceleration

The original wrapper at 0x10861C takes IFile in r0, output buffer in r1 and
output length pointer in r2. r1=0 size queries still execute in ARM. Successful
host calls return r0=0 to LR, preserve SP and callee-saved registers, write the
exact uncompressed bytes/length, and preserve the original read-ahead position:
a 13-byte header followed by complete 64 KiB fread blocks, bounded by EOF.
All 3,330 actual original routine calls establish this contract, including
multi-block maps and archive-tail resources. No guest program bytes are patched.

NativeLzma enables only for the exact original module and PACK SHA256 plus
wrapper words E92D4FF7/E24DD802/E8BD8FF0. Each call requires a read-only original
PACK handle with the same verified backing array and an indexed entry boundary.
It checks output bounds before any writes. Decode failure leaves guest memory
and file position untouched and executes the original routine. Unknown original
identities retain ARM decoding. XZ for Java 1.12 is bundled offline; official
source, license and binary/source hashes are retained in reference/. D8 consumes
the binary dependency; no platform-native decoder or online setup is required.

Read-only FileState handles now retain immutable filePayloads backing bytes.
Writable handles clone them, and an unexpected write to a read-only shared
handle detaches its bytes before mutation, preserving previous copy isolation.
This avoids repeatedly allocating/copying all 52,532,706 archive bytes per open.
No original file contents or save formats are changed.

Decoded assets use a per-session access-order 8 MiB memory cache and optional
32 MiB app-private disk cache. Disk namespace includes the full PACK SHA256;
keys contain entry offset/packed length. Records validate magic, output length,
exact file size and output SHA256, and writes rename a complete temporary file.
Corrupt/truncated records are removed and decoded again. Cache storage failures
are ignored; no saves or runtime snapshots are cached. Android may evict it.

Reports include host decoder/cache counters and time, fallbacks, avoided file
copy volume and first-gameplay time since launch. The latter includes menus and
user input and is explicitly labelled; it is not isolated map-load timing.
The existing gameplay/fire-held frame timing and touch controls are retained.

title: Correct native buttons and fine touch input
text:
The running original ARM callbacks prove the face masks: UID 0106C40B -> 0001
(ZEEBO_1/203), UID 0106C40A -> 0002 (ZEEBO_2/204), UID 0106C40D -> 0004
(ZEEBO_3/205), UID 0106C40C -> 0008 (ZEEBO_4/206). The former inherited
2/4 UID assignment was reversed. Original menu Back is key 204/button 2;
button 1 confirms. All thirteen face/shoulder/secondary controls are checked
for their exact native mask and clean release by QuakeControlProbe.

ControlsState reads this exact edition's relocated keybinding table at
0x82D438 and original key_dest at 0x1FA914. It does not write either. Labels
track the actual commands rather than guessing Casual/Expert from a saved
preference. FIRE · DRAG resolves the native UID bound to +attack. Context or
binding changes release touch contacts before changing the captions/routing.

The floating MOVE origin starts at the contact point. A continuous 6% radial
deadzone and curved magnitude replace the previous discontinuous 12% cutoff.
The original HID helper itself suppresses stick changes below 25%. Touch mode
retains it for menu navigation, and supplies continuous virtual samples through
the unchanged NBI adapter only at the original IN_Move poll (0x10E22C), after
the original has calculated frame speed. Every original instruction still runs.
The suspended ARM registers, flags, instruction mode and current PC are restored
after the adapter calls. No original code, binding, angle or position is patched.

NBI axis events E024/E023/E028/E027 deliver left X/Y and right X/Y in the
original fixed-point format. Touch look accumulates relative distances (0.22
reference degrees per dp at the original default sensitivity), sampled once at
the original poll. Conversion uses the original frame speed and axis-mode flags.
The game still applies its sensitivity, inversion, view clamp and actual preset.
Swipe impulses can reach 3x virtual deflection for quick turns; pending look is
bounded to 18 degrees. Stationary touch does not hold a turning velocity. A
1 dp native test changes yaw by about -0.214 degrees, below one degree and in
the original rightward direction. Menu motion is discarded. Cancel, pause,
resize, preset changes and restart clear contact/motion state.

title: Original side-move arithmetic and separate fire-held timing
text:
The original Joy_AdvancedUpdate at 0x1835C0 chooses AxisTurn (4) for left X in
Casual, and AxisSide (3) in Expert. The touch device now selects the already
compiled AxisSide path for left X during IN_Move. At 0x10E22C it saves the
current horizontal-axis descriptor at 0x82B394 and temporarily supplies 3.
At the common original epilogue (0x10E9C4), it captures the real forward/side
usercmd fields and restores the saved descriptor before the original returns.
Original instructions continue executing, including the original strafe
arithmetic. The original preset cvar and numbered/shoulder binding table are
retained; no original code, player coordinates or camera angles are written.
The exact entry/epilogue/adapter instruction words are checked when touch mode
is enabled. The native test proves both strafe directions without yaw change,
restored descriptor/preset/bindings, and forward + strafe + look + fire together.

AIM is now one ViewGroup containing an 88 dp fire target. Its touch router owns
all pointer IDs within that surface and selects firing only from a contact's
initial hit. Look-only contacts can cross the target without firing. A firing
contact keeps its own shared BridgeInput source while dragging outside the
button. Additional aim/fire contacts use distinct IDs; the newest aim contact
owns look, and superseded contacts cannot release another contact's key hold.
Accessibility taps still use the actual embedded Android Button. Original
fire buttons retain their drag behavior. All original controls and shared UI
1.1.2 remain present. Both supplied integration kits remain unchanged.

Reference swipe gain remains 0.22 degrees/dp horizontally and is now 0.14
vertically, still translated into native input samples before the original's
sensitivity/inversion/view clamp. No averaging filter is introduced.

AndroidEglDriver calls a swap observer with monotonic wall time, readback plus
pixel-conversion duration, and actual swap success. FrameTiming groups only
consecutive successful swaps in active original gameplay (key_dest game and
connection state active, original refresh_prepped byte set and loading-plaque
byte clear). The original CL_Frame and loading-plaque instructions establish
these fields. Menus, loading and Android lifecycle gaps break the
interval chain. A second category requires the original fire binding to be
held at both endpoints. The report explicitly calls this fire-held gameplay,
not enemy/combat detection. It includes a bounded rolling 10-second window,
interval p50/p95/max, FPS, capture mean cost and cumulative active-category FPS.
Reports remain cached and exported by the independent writer; new filenames
correctly identify v0.1.3. Native input/fire-state classification, timing math
and the production swap observer have separate tests. These metrics have not
yet been measured on a physical phone with v0.1.3.

title: The rejected control screen omitted simultaneous contacts
text:
This update replaces the rejected generic control screen with Carbon-owned left/right thumb groups. `README_FIRST.txt` contains install/control/test scope and known issues. The original CPU, guest logic, assets, graphics/audio compatibility and owner signer are preserved. The only portable runtime addition is a read-only control-preset accessor.

## Input and layout changes

`CarbonControls` is a game-owned ViewGroup using the real shared v1.1.2 `BridgeDigitalPad` with `withDiagonals(true)` and owned `BridgeInput.Source` action buttons. The original v0.1.0 integration omitted simultaneous-cardinal mode, causing the pad to reject a second contact. This bridge now enables it in both panels. Independent contact ownership, slide/re-entry, opposite direction holds, action combinations and release/cancel behavior are tested through actual Android MotionEvent dispatch.

The normal panel places the square pad under the left thumb, labeled accelerator/brake under the right, and nitro/handbrake nearby. 3/4/PAUSE remain available. Preset B relocates the original 1/3 auxiliary keys while preserving native OK and Back access. Native identifiers remain beneath action labels. `CarbonControls.Key` is game-owned, but all touch/hardware ownership stays in the shared input state; dynamic rebinding releases touch owners and preserves physical UID holds. Each button retains every pointer and drops missing/cancelled contacts. Haptic press feedback is retained.

A visible shared inline ORIGINAL Z-PAD / DRIVING CONTROLS switch preserves all original buttons and the same live renderer/viewport. It neither recreates nor restarts the game. Saved state retains mode only. Both panels have the same measured slot and wing geometry.

The private v1.1.2 UI source has bounded opt-in additions: `fitNativeViewport`, `flankingLandscape`, `controlModeNames`, and `BridgeFlankingControls`. Stock defaults and input models are unchanged. Carbon's portrait frame fits the native 4:3 image while controls stay bottom-aligned at a bounded preferred height. Spare portrait room stays outside the frame. Landscape gives game-owned controls two transparent-center wings, with the native-aspect viewport between them and the shared mode button below the picture. No game-obscuring overlay, crop/stretch, forced immersive mode or target/font shrinking is used. This is a local integration addition, not a new generic kit release. Full shared release-gate evidence covers the actual shipped modified JAR.

## Verification

The eight Carbon API34 Android framework scenarios include 48 geometry cases (A/B, two modes, six phone/tablet orientation sizes, font 1.0/1.3), target and text bounds, square D-pad and clear picture, actual root dispatch for two pad contacts plus accelerator through all six release orders in both modes/orientations, other direction pairs/opposites, sliding, nitro, cancellation, inline switch, physical ownership, preset changes, insets, resize, pause/Back, report wiring and isolated state/recovery. The modified shared UI JAR passed all 12 Android framework scenarios plus its existing host input/pad/geometry/configuration checks. `evidence/shared-ui-release-gate.txt` pins its SHA256. The original 28 focused compatibility checks still pass.

`CarbonLifecycleProbe` uses actual compiled APK runtime classes and original ARM mapper 0x00102F88. It checks Up + Right + accelerator as distinct native press descriptors, independent release order, held-set preservation, no fabricated extra event, and read-only native default-preset A. This is an input contract, not race driving. It then verifies cold EVT_APP_STOP/CloseApplet with real Mesa swaps and no remaining runnable guest. No runtime fault occurred in that contract.

Final package validation covers every original hash, complete strict-v1 assets/resources/native inventory, ZIP integrity, APK v2/v3 signatures, and identical owner signer for update installation. title: Leaving the original race still faults

## Newly observed unresolved runtime path

During native options navigation, original pause-menu SAIR followed by SIM caused `thread -> RuntimeException: MEM OOB F0001024+1` at 2,075,634,748 guest instructions. `evidence/original-menu-investigation/` preserves the input trace, screenshots and GL totals. This update does not repair that path. The passing cold-stop contract is separate and must not be generalized to all in-race exit paths.

## Continuity

The original ZIP, module class 0x0108C0BC, legacy IGL/IEGL ABI, 128MiB mapped RAM/64MiB heap fix, exact OES signed-byte coordinate conversion, palette/ATC codec, independent Downloads writer, native pause UID 0x0106C403, host-clock suspension, isolated state, audio backend and strict Omni metadata are retained. Full engine/MIDI/effects semantics, console timbre, save/load, campaign, Config C analog, memory/performance audit and production Omni acceptance remain open. Do not enable inherited Quake-specific touch/loading helpers. Keep this entire checkpoint, originals, source, tools and signing material private.

title: Quake’s runtime meets Carbon’s legacy graphics ABI
text:
This fork adapts the owner's preserved Quake II Zeebo Java ARM/Thumb runtime to the original Carbon applet class 0x0108C0BC and module `mod/276121/nfs.mod`. The 128 MiB mapped memory and 64 MiB heap allocation region avoid the original service tables/stacks and accommodate the 15,518,924-byte original allocation. The broader memory/free-RAM model still needs auditing.

`LegacyGraphicsAbi` translates Carbon's legacy IGL/IEGL method tables. Unlike the newer interface, these calls use r0 as the first C argument, have no interface-this argument, and return directly. Legacy GL slots translate to the preserved internal GLES method vocabulary, including ninth stack arguments. Android owns a real EGL14 ES1 context and 640x480 pbuffer on the guest worker. Its readback becomes the original-aspect Canvas image. There is no simulated racing engine or fabricated scene.

The former red stippled car artifact came from GL_BYTE texture coordinates. Desktop GL rejected the original OES byte-coordinate type. The verified fix expands each signed byte component to its exact non-normalized floating-point value, respecting interleaved stride. `ClientArrays` applies the same conversion in Android for vertices/texture coordinates. Normal and RGBA color arrays retain their original type/normalization. Android also implements Carbon's normal arrays, fixed-point lighting/material and other observed fixed-function operations. Unsupported calls remain visible failures. Only base GLES1 extensions are exposed to the guest; Android-only extension strings must not change original asset selection into an unimplemented path.

`ZeeboTextureCodec` retains original ATC formats and the OES 4/8-bit palette formats. Four-bit palettes use high nibble first and 16-bit colors little endian. Negative bundled-mipmap uploads are still unsupported and not advertised. Native paths observed in accepted runs use the original base fallback.

Two independent clean-render runs each completed 44,906 draws / 1,294 swaps with zero GL errors. The pause/resume run completed 70,583 draws / 1,488 swaps, 2,663,535,902 guest instructions and zero GL errors, with an actual race capture at 175 km/h. This is desktop Mesa evidence; it is not phone FPS or Android GPU proof.

title: Original engine audio remains experimental
text:
## Audio

Media objects retain their class IDs, including MP3 0x01005502 and MIDIOUTMSG 0x01005505. Original MIDI buffers are sampled when the guest actually requests Play. GameAudio routes original file media through MediaPlayer and reports actual starts/completions/errors back on the guest owner. Original MIDI message bytes can go to the Apache-licensed MidiDriver 1.29 Sonivox backend. Its arm64 release includes libc++/Oboe; all three ELF libraries have 16 KiB LOAD alignment. Extraction is enabled in the manifest. Licenses, release AAR and upstream source snapshot are retained privately.

No full engine-audio success is claimed. The observed 30-byte MIDIOUTMSG setup includes original program/control/note messages, but complete dynamic command, sample-bank, effects and notification semantics remain to investigate. Built-in Sonivox timbres are not a verified console bank. The desktop audio contract mode synthesizes only START callback timing and explicitly has no audible sink; it must never be reported as audible playback.

title: Katamari foundation loads the game’s own Micro3D module
text:
Base: Katamari v0.1.0 CPU/BREW interpreter and Genesis-style Android presentation. No unrelated game is packaged.

The original game module maps at 0x00100000. Its CreateInstance comparison establishes class ID 0x010279D7. title: First-minigame acceptance and its save boundary
text:
## Verification and limits

- 74 original-game host checks passed, including unchanged game/Micro3D startup, all 20 native input latches/releases, menus/Help, Web Climber, motion/jump, native MIDI, 1224 callbacks and save serialization/reload.
- 18 actual production-controller checks passed: scheduled deadlines, no input-driven timers, short taps, separate 5/OK, background release/suspension and resume.
- 5,375 Spider-Man mapping/contact/geometry assertions passed across 28 device/density/orientation cases.
- All twelve shared Android framework tests passed against the locally rebuilt v1.1.2 JAR; its compiled classes exactly match the shared classes compiled into this APK.
- Seven integrated Android API 34 framework tests passed against the production Activity and APK resources, using actual Window/View/graphics/MotionEvent callbacks. Covered cold startup, safe areas, complete controls, stable renderer/modes, two-pointer sliding/action input, both release orders and the center guard in both modes, hardware ownership, duplicate 5 ownership, independent report callback, Back/cleanup, dialog key-up and startup fault recording. The real report writer also completed while the guest worker was blocked, correctly reported an intentionally unavailable Downloads destination, and retained its fallback/fault files.
- APK original payload hashes, unchanged runtime source, signing continuity, DEX/icon packaging, signature and alignment passed.

The Activity tests isolate/defer the guest boundary; they do not simulate game progress. Host UI previews replay a framebuffer produced by actual original-game host execution, not a phone capture. Gameplay evidence is separate in evidence/acceptance/.

Not observed: physical phone launch/touch comfort/fit, audible phone playback, live successful Downloads export on a phone, phone heat, a full playthrough or later minigames. The save serializer was directly invoked on existing native score fields to test its genuine original file path; this does not establish a naturally earned completed-level save.

title: Original file-seek and key-event contracts
text:
Compatibility added from observed calls:

- BREW memory availability for this ABI: GetDeviceInfo memory field +24 and RAM allocation availability +0x18.
- SYS_B +0xE4 ASCII-to-wide conversion, bounded by source length and destination byte capacity.
- This title's IFile seek origins: 0=start, 1=end, 2=current; successful Seek returns the position. This is required for its original ZIP parser and original in-module decompressor. The original parser reads `res.dat`; no host replacement of game archive parsing is used.
- Original 176x220 device surface matches the fixed 176x190 scene resources plus contextual footer. Display does not crop/stretch the framebuffer.
- Host font raster and IDisplay.DrawText for original strings; palette/text/background colors retained.
- Observed zero graphics translation and graphics hint calls.
- IShell MIME-header detection for MIDI and MIDI media-handler class selection, letting original game code create IMedia and submit the unchanged original stream.
- Separate original Micro3D instruction counter for reports/evidence.

The original event handler at 0x1185E0 maps EVT_KEY 0x100 to its key latches and EVT_KEY_RELEASE 0x102 to the release function. EVT_KEY_PRESS 0x101 does not take that latch route. Numeric keys, 5, OK, all arrows, both softkeys, CLR, star and pound retain distinct native identities.

Production key releases shorter than one guest callback are deferred until that callback has run at its actual registered deadline. Input does not pump or shorten timers. Background focus loss immediately releases all physical and deferred keys and cancels host callbacks.

One game worker owns guest execution, native timers, audio callbacks and save persistence. A separate report executor copies already published evidence to Downloads via MediaStore on Android 10+; reports never acquire the runtime lock. Routine tracing stays OFF. Changed pixel revisions drive UI redraw. Battery/thermal samples are sparse (>=15 seconds); they are not CPU/GPU/skin measurements.

title: A center contact stays a center contact
text:
This pass applies Wakka Bridge Gameplay UI Kit v1.1.2: actual game icon/title, BREW platform beneath the title, independent SAVE REPORT and three-dot utilities; a square sliding four-way D-pad; distinct center OK and prominent 5; both softkeys and Clear; direct ORIGINAL KEYPAD / D-PAD RETURN switching.

Both layouts reserve the same measured slot: switching does not change the live renderer, viewport bounds, worker, original timers or game session. Spider-Man opts into one local kit extension preserving v0.1.0's center-contact ownership: a directional contact crossing the center does not press OK; a center contact does not turn into movement. The upstream v1.1.2 behavior remains the default for configurations that do not opt in. Guard ownership is now retained per stable pointer ID, without reverting the new contact union. title: The original clock spins while the logo waits
text:
EXECUTION
All original game methods run as Java/Dex against a targeted MIDP layer.
Original assets remain byte-identical. No gameplay is reimplemented.
D8 keeps bridge/MIDP/UI code in the main DEX. Original classes are separate
prepared assets: guest.dex from the unchanged JAR, and clock.dex from d.class.
GuestLoader loads clock.dex before guest.dex in one guest class namespace;
all original reflection uses Platform.guestClass. Android/MIDP stays in the
parent loader. Content-addressed code-cache copies are read-only before loading.
Resources are packaged at the APK classpath root, preserving resource lookup.
The supplied original JAR is retained unchanged under original/game.jar.

One explicit platform API redirect is applied to d.class in a generated JAR:
System.currentTimeMillis() becomes bridge.GameClock.currentTimeMillis(),
which delegates to the unchanged blocking Platform clock. The constant
pool method owner changes; every original instruction, method body and all
other constant-pool entries remain intact. tools/prepare_game.py owns this.
The original d.run() repeatedly polls time without sleeping, including during
3-second logos. The host clock blocks for 1 ms per poll and gates on foreground
state. It returns real wall time and keeps the original per-scene q deadlines
(75 ms rooftops, 115 ms subway, 68 ms first boss in the tested states).
The separate original gameplay clock calls outside d.class remain unchanged.
A host comparison of the actual logo timer found 99.97% of one CPU core for
original busy waiting and 1.60% with the blocking host clock; first-logo pixels
were identical. This is timer-thread host evidence, not phone thermal evidence.

title: Separate prepared guest classes and generic reconstruction

OMNI 0.5.7 STRICT HANDOFF — v0.1.2
The build embeds omni-game/import/export properties and omni-preparation.json.
handoff-plan.json is generated from the exact original and APK inventory.
The whole original JAR is explicitly private original data. All 67 original

to d.class's same-length UTF8 owner, and runs the unmodified production D8
compiler twice in mode none. Expected class inventory is pinned for all 19
original classes and the separate d.class overlay; resource bytes are exact.
